lines.text: Lines fifty-eight to seventy-eight are the fields, the command's memory.
Blue goal: a fixed goal, written for blue. Goal supplier: a goal that can move. Blue next: the next waypoint.
Then the tolerances, two centimeters and two degrees, and end speed and switch radius: zero, unless it's a waypoint.
Lines seventy to seventy-three build the request: a closed-loop field velocity, so even slow final moves happen.
Line seventy-five, commanded: the last velocity we asked for. The speed rule's only memory.
Lines seventy-seven and seventy-eight start distance and heading error at infinity: not there yet.
Line eighty-five takes a fixed goal. Its Javadoc says: always write it for the blue alliance.
Line ninety-three takes a supplier: a small function returning a fresh goal, already in field coordinates, so never flipped.
Line ninety-eight is protected, for subclasses like Drive To Tag that bring their own goal.
All of them reach line one hundred four, which names the command and claims the drivetrain.
